title: Law of conservation of mass
competency: State the law of conservation of mass.

keywords.def: Matter is neither created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction.

en.text: The law of conservation of mass says matter is neither created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction. The mass of the reactants equals the mass of the products. Burning paper seems to lose mass only because gases escape into the air.

screens.title: Lighter ash
screens.ask: Paper burns. The ash is lighter than the paper. Was mass destroyed?
opts: No, gases escaped into the air
screens.after: Burning makes gases that float away. If you caught them, the total mass would be the same.

screens.title: 3.3.3 Law of conservation of mass
paras: Matter is neither created nor destroyed during a chemical reaction.
The mass of the reactants is exactly equal to the mass of the products.

screens.title: Key words
defs: Matter is neither created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction.

screens.text: What does the law of conservation of mass say?
opts: Mass is lost when things burn
Matter is neither created nor destroyed in a reaction
screens.ans: Matter is neither created nor destroyed in a reaction

screens.text: In a chemical reaction atoms are neither created nor destroyed.
screens.why: This is the law of conservation of mass.

screens.ask: 10 g of reactants react completely. The products have a mass of ___ g.
screens.why: Mass of reactants = mass of products.
screens.clue: Mass is not lost or gained.

screens.ask: In a closed bottle, 24 g of magnesium burns with 16 g of oxygen. The magnesium oxide has a mass of ___ g.
screens.why: Reactants: 24 + 16 = 40 g. Mass is conserved, so the product is 40 g.
screens.clue: Add the masses of the reactants.
